name: Laravel Eloquent mass-assignment protection disabled
attack_scenario: A signup or profile-update request adds `is_admin=1` (or `role`, `balance`, `email_verified_at`, `account_id`); with mass-assignment protection off, Eloquent binds and persists it, letting the attacker escalate privileges, seize another tenant's records, or flip verification/balance fields the endpoint never intended to expose.
negative_test_hint: register with the extra field "is_admin=1" in the request body and assert it is ignored and never persisted because the model whitelists attributes via $fillable

exemplar.explanation: `protected $guarded = []` and `Model::unguard()` disable Eloquent's mass-assignment protection, so a request smuggling in is_admin, role, or balance fields gets bound and persisted — privilege escalation or cross-tenant data seizure. Whitelisting with `$fillable` ensures only intended attributes can ever be assigned from request data.
